# pqtransport

Pure-Dart post-quantum transport for Dart and Flutter.

- Package: https://github.com/turkananation/pqtransport
- Docs: https://github.com/turkananation/pqtransport/blob/main/doc/INDEX.md
- Claim boundary: https://github.com/turkananation/pqtransport/blob/main/doc/CLAIM_BOUNDARY.md
- Crypto: package:pqforge ^0.4.5 (ML-KEM, ML-DSA, AES-256-GCM, dart2js-safe ChaCha, X25519, P-256/P-384 ECDH, RFC 5869 HKDF)
- Infra: package:swissarmyknife (Result, StateMachine, CircuitBreaker, Cache)
- No dart:ffi. No platform TLS on the PQ path.
- Live handshake in 0.1.0: all three RFC 10024 groups (X25519MLKEM768, SecP256r1MLKEM768, SecP384r1MLKEM1024). P-384 requires PqForgeProfile.maximum. Profile/group mismatches fail closed (requireGroup).
- TLS encoding is RFC 8446-shaped ClientHello/ServerHello (OPEN-01 done). Compact 0.1 body retired. Cipher IANA 0x1302 (SHA-384 AES-GCM, default) and 0x1303 (ChaCha). Certificate is still raw ML-DSA-65; raw-pk is negotiated (OPEN-04). HelloRetryRequest is on the wire with cookie (OPEN-05). Not OpenSSL-interop.
- Record schedule follows the suite: HKDF-SHA-384 for 0x1302, HKDF-SHA-256 for 0x1303. OPEN-02 and OPEN-13 are Fixed. dart2js fail-closes 0x1303 (PointyCastle Poly1305 needs 64-bit integers); AES-GCM 0x1302 is the web suite.
- Not a FIPS 140 module.

Start at doc/INDEX.md. Do not invent FIPS/CMVP, constant-time, or erasure claims.
